{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Read data again
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean revenue (though not needed for this question)
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter for loyal customers AND completed status only
# Because: 'converted' is 1 even for refunded orders, so we must use 'status' == 'completed' to define conversion
# The question asks for 'converted' meaning 'completed checkout', so only 'completed' orders count

# Define conversion as: completed checkout (status == 'completed')
df_loyal_completed = df[(df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & (df['status'] == 'completed')]

# Count total loyal completed orders
n_loyal_completed = len(df_loyal_completed)

# Count converted (i.e., completed) loyal orders
# Since we've filtered to 'completed', all are converted by definition
n_converted_loyal = n_loyal_completed  # All completed orders are conversions

# Compute fraction
frac_converted = n_converted_loyal / n_loyal_completed

print(f"Loyal customers with completed orders: {n_loyal_completed}")
print(f"Converted (completed) loyal orders: {n_converted_loyal}")
print(f"Conversion fraction: {frac_converted:.4f}")

frac_converted"}
